skill.name: routeros-container
skill.description: Guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through RouterOS container setup on MikroTik devices. Covers device-mode, VETH networking, storage, image import, lifecycle commands, REST API control, and /app comparisons.
skill.summary: Configure and manage OCI containers on MikroTik RouterOS devices.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: The static command, network, filesystem, obfuscation, and reconnaissance hits are mostly Markdown examples or reference links, not executable behavior in the skill. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found. One semantic issue remains: the REST API sample demonstrates plaintext Basic authentication with a default admin account.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the HTTP Basic example with HTTPS where available, a named least-privilege account, and a prompt for user-supplied credentials.
Replace values such as secret with guidance to generate unique passwords and avoid storing credentials in shared transcripts.
Recommend pinned tags or digests and image review before pulling public images onto RouterOS devices.

semantic_findings.title: Insecure RouterOS REST Authentication Example
semantic_findings.description: The REST API sample uses plaintext HTTP and builds a Basic auth header from the default admin account with an empty password. If copied unchanged, privileged router credentials and container control requests could be exposed on the local network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The adjacent lines directly show the HTTP endpoint and Basic credential construction. The risk depends on users copying the sample unchanged, but the unsafe pattern is explicit.

content.value_statement: RouterOS containers require device-mode, storage, VETH networking, and version-specific commands. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce safer MikroTik container workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS container prerequisites, device-mode confirmation, and package installation paths.
Builds VETH, bridge, NAT, and port-forwarding workflows for container networking.
Shows container environment variables, mounts, storage paths, and version-specific property names.
Guides image pulls, local tar imports, and RouterOS architecture mapping.
Outlines CLI and REST API lifecycle operations for list, start, stop, delete, and status checks.
Compares manual container setup with the RouterOS /app YAML system.
limitations: It does not verify commands against a live router unless a separate RouterOS tool is available.
It cannot guarantee third-party container images are safe or compatible.
Version details may need confirmation on RouterOS releases newer than the skill content.
It does not replace RouterOS backups, lab testing, or change-control procedures.

use_cases.title: Provision Edge Containers
use_cases.description: Plan RouterOS package setup, storage, VETH interfaces, bridges, NAT, and container lifecycle commands.

use_cases.title: Automate REST Lifecycle Tasks
use_cases.description: Design safer REST workflows for listing, starting, stopping, polling, and deleting RouterOS containers.

use_cases.title: Prepare Local Images
use_cases.description: Map RouterOS architecture to image platforms and check local tar import requirements before deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Check Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a MikroTik router running RouterOS [version] on [architecture]. Help me check whether it can run containers and list the safe setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create Container Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a VETH, bridge, IP, and NAT plan for a RouterOS container that should expose [service] on port [port]. Include rollback notes.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy an Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me deploy [image name] on RouterOS [version] using external storage [disk path]. Include env vars, mounts, and lifecycle commands.

prompt_templates.title: Automate with REST
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a least-privilege REST workflow for managing RouterOS containers from [language or tool]. Include polling, error handling, and credential safety.

output_examples.input: I need Pi-hole on a MikroTik router with external USB storage.
output: Prerequisite checklist for RouterOS version, package status, architecture, and storage.
VETH, bridge, gateway, NAT, and port-forwarding plan.
Container lifecycle sequence with environment variables and volume guidance.
Security notes for credentials, image trust, and rollback planning.

output_examples.input: I need to delete a container through the RouterOS REST API.
output_examples.output: A lifecycle plan that reads running status, stops the container, waits until stopped, deletes it, and reports errors.

output_examples.input: I need to build a local image tar for an ARM64 router.
output_examples.output: A compatibility checklist covering platform mapping, single-layer image format, uncompressed layers, and RouterOS import steps.

best_practices: Confirm RouterOS version and architecture before selecting package, image, and property names.
Use external storage for container roots and volumes to protect internal flash.
Use dedicated credentials, secure management networks, and backups before REST or firewall changes.
anti_patterns: Copying examples with default admin credentials or placeholder secrets.
Running containers from untrusted registries without pinning or review.
Changing device-mode, NAT, or bridge settings on production routers without a rollback plan.

faq.question: Does this skill install containers by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and guidance. The user or tool must execute them on a RouterOS device.

faq.question: Which RouterOS versions are covered?
faq.answer: It focuses on RouterOS 7.x and notes changes around 7.18, 7.20, 7.21, and 7.22.

faq.question: Does RouterOS run Docker directly?
faq.answer: No. RouterOS runs OCI-compatible containers through MikroTik /container features, with different image and networking rules.

faq.question: Can it help with REST API automation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains list, start, stop, delete, and status patterns, including string status values.

faq.question: What storage should I use?
faq.answer: Use external storage for image roots and persistent volumes. Internal flash can wear out quickly.

faq.question: Is /app YAML the same as manual containers?
faq.answer: No. /app YAML is more declarative. Manual setup gives more control over VETH, bridges, and Layer 2 access.
